THE SHAPE
---------
Everything that decides WHAT is shown or what a key MEANS is elsewhere and is tested with plain strings: render.py,
approval.py, diff.py, status.py, keys.py (C09a) and session.py (the controller).  This module only does terminal I/O

m2c/src/m2c/tui/approval.py -- Patch C09a: the approval prompt as a state machine, and what it remembers.

C24 (runner.py) calls an ``ask`` function with an ``ApprovalRequest`` and waits for a ``Choice``.  This module is the
pure part of the terminal's ``ask``: what the prompt shows (``describe_request``), what each key means
(``ApprovalMachine``), and the per-session memory (``SessionMemory``).  The prompt_toolkit layer only forwards keys
and shows blocks.

KEYS
----
``y`` allow once · ``a`` allow this EXACT call for the rest of the session (``Choice(scope="session")``; for
``plan_exit`` it is only ever once, like C24) · ``n`` deny · ``d`` deny AND do not ask again for this exact call in
this session · ``e`` edit (bash only: the command text goes to an editable buffer and comes back as
``Choice(edited_input=...)``) · ``v`` or Tab show the whole diff · Esc leaves the editor.  Any other key does
nothing: no key ever answers by accident, and a prompt that is dismissed (C24 cancels the ask task) answers nothing.

``d`` is realized in the UI on purpose: the plan lists ``d`` as "deny", but C24's ``Choice`` has no session-wide
deny (a deny with scope session is treated as once).  So the answer sent is a plain deny, ``Done.remember_deny``
tells the app to put the call in ``SessionMemory``, and a later identical call is answered with a deny at once,
without a prompt.  The memory lives in this process only.  ``SessionMemory`` also remembers ``a`` because the app
starts a new ``ToolRun

m2c/src/m2c/tui/complete.py -- Patch C09a: ``@`` file mentions.

Typing ``@`` in the message line completes project file paths.  It only INSERTS the relative path into the message;
it never reads or attaches contents.  What is offered is decided here (pure logic plus a bounded directory scan);
the prompt_toolkit ``Completer`` that calls it lives in app.py.

WHAT IS NEVER OFFERED
---------------------
* Anything C05's denylist blocks (``Denylist.blocks`` on the root-relative parts: ``.env``, keys, M2C's own state
  directory, the user's patterns), and the directory is not entered either.
* ``.git`` (and ``node_modules``, ``__pycache__``: they would use up the scan budget).
* Symbolic links of any kind (a link can point outside the project or at a protected file; the scan neither offers
  nor follows them).  Each candidate is also run through C05's ``resolve_for_read`` as a last check.
* Names with control or format characters (they would put hidden text into the message line).

BOUNDS
------
The scan stops after ``MAX_FILES`` files or ``TIME_BUDGET_S`` seconds, whichever comes first (the loop it runs on
also carries the device link), and a query returns at most ``MAX_CANDIDATES`` paths.  ``Scan.complete`` says whether
the whole tree was seen.

Standard library plus C05's path guard.

m2c/src/m2c/tui/diff.py -- Patch C09a: building a unified diff of a proposed edit and collapsing a large one.

A card for ``edit_file`` or ``write_file`` shows what would change.  This module decides WHAT (pure, no terminal, no
file access of its own): ``diff_for_call`` turns a call's input into a ``Diff``; ``collapse`` keeps the first few
lines of a long one and says how many are hidden; ``expand`` returns every line (still bounded).

* ``edit_file`` is shown as the change from ``old_string`` to ``new_string`` (the call carries no file text).
* ``write_file`` is shown against the file's current text when the caller can supply it (``read_existing``, which
  the app backs with C05's path guard so a protected file is never read here), else as all-new text.
* Work is bounded: inputs above ``MAX_INPUT_CHARS`` are not diffed line by line (difflib is quadratic in the worst
  case); a diff keeps at most ``MAX_DIFF_LINES`` lines and says so.  A huge change can therefore never stall the
  loop that also carries the device link.
* Every line is run through ``safe.clean`` (a file or a model can contain escape sequences).

Standard library only; pure.

m2c/src/m2c/tui/grant.py -- Patch C09a: asking for more credits when a run is paused for budget (``g``).

``POST /v1/code/runs/{run_id}/grant`` (S10) raises the run's credit ceiling when the run is in ``paused_budget`` and
the account's pool has room.  The device authenticates with its short-lived access token (C03's
``get_access_token()``); the answer is numbers and a state word.  This module makes that one call with the standard
library and turns every outcome into a ``GrantResult`` and one fixed sentence (``describe``).

SAFETY
------
* The token is revealed only to build the ``Authorization`` header; it is never logged, printed or put in a result.
* The server address is the credential's own, run through ``normalize_server_url`` (https, or http to loopback
  only); redirects are NOT followed (a redirect would carry the token elsewhere).
* Nothing the server sends is shown except numbers it must have sent as numbers, a state word of lowercase letters
  and a ``reset_at`` timestamp that matches a strict pattern.  Error ``message`` text is never shown.
* Credits only; no dollars.
* Blocking work (the token fetch and the HTTP call) runs in a thread so the loop that carries the device link keeps
  running.

OUTCOMES (``GrantResult.kind``)
-------------------------------
``granted`` · ``pool_exhausted`` (shows ``reset_at``) · ``device_offline`` · ``not_paused`` · ``run_gone`` (the server
lost the run's buffer: start a new run) · ``rate_limited`` · ``unavailable`` (503) · ``unau

m2c/src/m2c/tui/history.py -- Patch C09a: the conversation rebuilt from the local log, for ``run.start``'s ``history``.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
P00 has no softer interrupt than ``cancel``, and cancel ends the run.  The conversation is not lost, because the
device keeps it (C02): the next message starts a NEW run and passes ``history`` -- the protocol's history items --
rebuilt from the session's log.  The same happens after a rewind (C08), where the server's copy of the conversation
is out of step with the files.  This module is that rebuild.  It is pure: it reads a sequence of ``(type, data)``
pairs and returns history items; it touches no store and no terminal.

THE LOG CONVENTION (written by the app; ``repl.py`` already writes the first two)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
``user.message {text}`` · ``user.unsent {}`` (the last user message never reached the server) ·
``assistant.message {text}`` (one per model step, written at ``text_done``; a reply that was restarted is written
once, with its final text) · ``tool.call {call_id, tool, input}`` · ``tool.result {call_id, ok, output, truncated?,
trust?}`` (what the device sent back; the run's events carry no outputs) · ``tool.closed {call_id, status}`` (the
server's ``tool_finished``) · ``checkpoint {step, call_id?, tool?}`` (a C08 snapshot step, tied to its call) ·
``rewind {to_step}`` (written by ``checkpoints.rewind``).  Anything else in the log is ignored.

m2c/src/m2c/tui/render.py -- Patch C09a: turning a server event into display blocks.

This is the "what is shown" half of the terminal chat; app.py (a later patch) is the thin prompt_toolkit/rich layer
that prints the blocks.  Nothing here touches a terminal, a file or a clock, so every event type can be tested with
plain strings.

BLOCKS
------
``Block.kind`` is ``text`` (append to the current line: a streamed piece of the reply, no newline of its own),
``line`` (one whole line with a ``style``) or ``diff`` (the lines of a diff, collapsed or not).  Styles are names
(``plain dim info warning error user queued assistant tool ok bad``); the UI maps them to colors.

EVERY STRING IS CLEANED HERE
----------------------------
Text from the server, the model or a file goes through ``safe.clean`` before it is put in a block, so a UI that
prints blocks cannot show an escape sequence by forgetting to.  Tool and code names are restricted to a safe
alphabet.  Server error messages are never shown (fixed text per code, plus the code), because a message is free
text.

THE REPLY AND ``reply_restarted``
---------------------------------
``text_delta`` pieces are returned as they arrive.  ``reply_restarted`` (a notice from the server: the reply is
being written again after a dropped connection) closes the current line, forgets the partial reply and returns one
short line.  Terminal scrollback cannot be un-printed, so the discarded text stays above that line; what is
discarded is the renderer'

m2c/src/m2c/tui/safe.py -- Patch C09a: making untrusted text safe to show in a terminal.

EVERYTHING THE SERVER OR THE MODEL SENDS IS UNTRUSTED TEXT
----------------------------------------------------------
A model can be steered by a file it read, and a server is only as trustworthy as its last deploy.  Text that reaches
a terminal can recolor it, move the cursor, rewrite earlier lines, set the window title, make a hyperlink or hide
what a command really says (bidirectional overrides).  Every string that came from the server, the model or a file
therefore goes through ``clean`` before it is displayed, and is never handed to a markup interpreter
(``escape_markup`` exists for any caller that must).  The renderer (render.py) does this once, at the door, so no
display code can forget it.

What ``clean`` removes: ANSI/VT escape sequences (CSI, OSC, DCS/SOS/PM/APC, two-character escapes, and the 8-bit C1
forms), every control character except newline and tab (a lone carriage return becomes a newline: it would
overwrite the line), DEL, C1 controls, bidirectional controls and every other "format" character (zero-width
characters, joiners), and lone surrogates.  It never raises and never returns a character that a terminal could
act on.  An escape sequence split across two streamed pieces leaves at most harmless printable letters behind.

Standard library only; pure; no I/O.

Place this file at: m2c/src/m2c/tui/safe.py

m2c/src/m2c/tui/session.py -- Patch C09b: the session controller, the client wiring behind the terminal chat.

WHAT THIS IS
------------
``Session`` joins the pieces C09a made (render, approval, status, history, complete, grant) to the pieces the earlier
patches made (the device link C04, the tool runner C24, the policy engine C06, tools C05/C07, checkpoints C08, the
local store C02, the context loader C12).  It has NO terminal code: everything it shows goes through the small
``UI`` protocol (app.py), so the whole flow is tested with a fake UI against C04's fake server, and the prompt_toolkit
layer stays thin.

ONE LOOP, ONE LINK.  Everything runs on the single asyncio loop that carries the ``DeviceLink``.  The store connection
belongs to that thread (C24 says so too).  Link callbacks are synchronous and quick; slow work is a task.

THE CONVERSATION AND ITS RUNS
-----------------------------
P00 has no softer interrupt than ``cancel``, and cancel ends the run; a rewind leaves the server's copy of the
conversation out of step with the files; a run parked for budget or an error takes no more messages.  So a
conversation is a CHAIN of runs, and the device keeps the conversation:

* the CONVERSATION SESSION (one row in the C02 ``sessions`` table, made at startup) holds the client events C09a's
  ``history.py`` reads -- ``user.message``, ``user.unsent``, ``assistant.message``, ``tool.call``, ``tool.result``,
  ``tool.closed``, ``checkpoint`` -- plus what C24 and C08 write for it (

m2c/src/m2c/tui/status.py -- Patch C09a: the status line, and the live mode cycle.

``StatusState`` is what the status line knows; ``observe`` folds one server event into it; ``format_status`` and
``status_lines`` turn it into text.  Pure: no terminal, no clock, no I/O.

WHAT THE LINE SHOWS
-------------------
mode · the model (its quality class when known, else the model id of the last usage event) · the TAINTED flag, only
when it is true (C17 comes later, so it is always false for now) · the context percentage · the credits spent in this
run (and the session total when it differs) · "working" and the number of queued messages.  Credits only: no
dollars anywhere.

THE CONTEXT PERCENTAGE IS AN ESTIMATE
-------------------------------------
It is the ``input_tokens`` of the LAST usage event over a window size (a constant, ``M2C_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS`` can
override it, an unusable value is ignored).  The text says ``~`` and the second line says "approximate".  The server
compacts the context itself, so this is a hint, not a guarantee.

THE QUALITY CLASS
-----------------
The protocol has no quality-class field.  The class reaches a client only inside the fixed text of the
``model_changed`` notice ("... so a <class> model is answering instead."); ``observe`` reads it with a strict
pattern (lowercase letters, at most 24).  Anything else leaves it unknown.  A protocol field would be better; that
is a note for the protocol owner, not something this patch invents.
